segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Hello and welcome to Real Easy English. In this podcast, we have real conversations in

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: easy English to help you learn. I'm Neil.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: And I'm Beth. Remember, you can find a script for this episode to read along on our website,

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: bbclearningenglish.com.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Hello Beth, how are you?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: I'm very well, Neil. How are you?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I'm good, thank you.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Good. What are we talking about in this episode, Neil?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Well, we are going to be talking about jobs and our careers.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: OK. So, can you explain the difference between a job and a career?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yes. So, our job is what we do for work.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: So, I work at BBC Learning English. It's my job.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: But career is a word we use to talk more about our work in the long term.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: So, all of the jobs that we've had and the jobs that we might want to do in the future.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: OK And also with career it a word we use to talk about the type of work we do So you might have a career in teaching or a career in TV for example

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: So, Neil, I know you work here at BBC Learning English, of course, but have you had any other jobs?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Oh yes, I've had lots of other jobs. Before I worked at the BBC, I was a teacher,

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: an English teacher. And before that, I had lots of jobs when I was a student.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: OK. So, how long have you worked at the BBC for?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: 20 years. More than 20 years.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Oh, wow. OK. So, when you were a student and you had jobs, that was quite a long time ago.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: It was ages ago, Beth, before the internet was invented.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: OK. And what jobs did you do when you were a student?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: So when I was a student, I worked in a hotel. I worked in restaurants as a waiter. I worked in a fish and chip shop.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Did you?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yeah.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: How long did you work in a fish and chip shop for?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I worked in a fish and chip shop for a summer. And how about you, Beth? When did you start working at the BBC?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: I have worked here for around three years So I been here since 2021 But I been working in London for six years because I been here since 2018

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: So Beth, you said that you have worked at the BBC since 2021.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Since.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: What does it mean when we use since?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Well, we use since followed by a date or a point in time.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: And we use it to talk about when something started.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: But also it's something that is still true.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: So I have been here since 2021 and I still work here now.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: So it's still true.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yeah. And that's different to for, isn't it?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: When you say, I've worked here for 20 years, we're talking about the length of time.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Exactly. And that can be something that is still true.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: For example, you've worked here for 20 years and you still work here now,

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: but it also could be something in the past.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: So, for example, you said you worked in a fish and chip shop for a summer

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: and that summer has a length of time. It has a start and an end.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yeah.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: So what is the funniest thing that ever happened at work Beth

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Well when I was a teenager I worked at a farm and sometimes the goats would escape

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: So I had to run after baby goats and I would have to pick them up and put them back.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: But I got a little cuddle with a baby goat.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: So it was funny, but it was also very nice.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Ah, that's a nice thing to do in your job.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Right, let's recap the words we've learnt today.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: We had career, which means the jobs we've had over time.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Since, which we use to talk about the time when something started.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: For, which we can use to talk about a length of time.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: For example, I've worked at the BBC for 20 years.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: That's it for this episode of Real Easy English.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: If you enjoyed this podcast, you can find more activities and courses to help you with your English

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: on our website

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: bbclearningenglish.com

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Next time, we'll be talking about our habits and daily routines.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: See you then. Goodbye.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Bye.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: you
